newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador sees 4 pct to 5 pct GDP growth for '97.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador sees 4 pct to 5 pct GDP growth for '97.

text.p: The government of El Salvador is predicting macroeconomic stability with solid growth and low inflation in 1997, the president of the Central Bank said Thursday.
Roberto Orellana told a news conference that gross domestic product was seen growing between four percent and five percent next year with inflation of between six percent and eight percent.
For 1996, the government is expecting GDP growth of between three percent and four percent and inflation between eight percent and nine percent, Orellana said.
"This year has been a correction for the economy," Orellana said.
The Salvadoran economy boomed immediately following a 1992 peace agreement that put an end to a 12-year-long civil war, slowing down only this year.
Orellana added that there would be no devaluation of the colon, the Salvadoran currency, in 1997.
"Stability in the economy has been achieved," Orellana said.
